<!-- @manual-start intro -->
# Leyman

An Nx monorepo of TypeScript libraries and tools for Node.js ESM environments. Documentation: [jacobley.github.io/leyman](https://jacobley.github.io/leyman/).

> **First time here?** Open this repo in VSCode — it will prompt you to reopen in the [DevContainer](.devcontainer/), which sets up Node, PNPM, and all tooling automatically. Day-to-day work happens in git worktrees; see the [worktrees skill](./.agents/skills/worktrees/SKILL.md).
<!-- @manual-end intro -->

## Demos

<!-- @manual-start demos -->
Worked examples of putting open-source projects and services together well, in [`demos/`](./demos). They are never published: the code and its write-up are the point. Each is tested against real services (devcontainer sidecars, and the same images in CI) with 100% coverage, and where a demo has several moving parts, they compose at runtime behind [haywire](./tools/haywire) bindings so each can be tested on its own. Also on the [docs site](https://jacobley.github.io/leyman/demos/).
<!-- @manual-end demos -->

| Demo                                                                              | What it shows                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Source                                                   |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| [BLAKE3 through WASM](https://jacobley.github.io/leyman/demos/blake3-wasm/)       | BLAKE3 from Rust through WASM with SIMD, on Node.js and in browsers, blocking or in a worker, measured against the fastest JavaScript to find where WASM pays off.                                                                     | [`demos/blake3-wasm`](./demos/blake3-wasm)               |
| [BLAKE3 from Go through WASM](https://jacobley.github.io/leyman/demos/blake3-go/) | The same Rust crate called from Go with no cgo: a C ABI built to bare WASM, run by wazero, and measured against BLAKE3 in Go and native Rust to find where it pays off.                                                                | [`demos/blake3-go`](./demos/blake3-go)                   |
| [Read-through cache](https://jacobley.github.io/leyman/demos/read-through-cache/) | BentoCache on Valkey: a memory tier kept in sync, stale-while-revalidate, one load per key across instances, and sharding over several nodes with weighted rendezvous hashing.                                                         | [`demos/read-through-cache`](./demos/read-through-cache) |
| [OpenAPI](https://jacobley.github.io/leyman/demos/openapi/)                       | A notes API from spec to database: an OpenAPI 3.1 document built from Juniper schemas, genever types for a typed client and a Hono server that validates every request and response, and Drizzle on Postgres with a database per test. | [`demos/openapi`](./demos/openapi)                       |
| [MCP server](https://jacobley.github.io/leyman/demos/mcp-server/)                 | Making the notes API easy for AI agents that connect to services: tools shaped for tasks, an OAuth resource server with step-up scopes, and token exchange to call the API as the agent’s user.                                        | [`demos/agents/mcp`](./demos/agents/mcp)                 |
| [CLI for agents](https://jacobley.github.io/leyman/demos/agent-cli/)              | Making the notes API easy for AI agents with a shell: one short command per task, logging in once from the API’s URL, with tokens, refresh and errors handled inside.                                                                  | [`demos/agents/cli`](./demos/agents/cli)                 |
| [Local ingress](https://jacobley.github.io/leyman/demos/local-ingress/)           | A Vite dev server behind one machine-wide Caddy: every worktree at its own https://&lt;worktree>.&lt;repo>.localhost, with a locally trusted certificate, hot reload through the proxy, and tunnels for phones.                        | [`demos/local-ingress`](./demos/local-ingress)           |

## Getting Started

```bash
# Install dependencies
pnpm i

# Build and test everything
test-ci
```

> **Nx is not globally installed.** It ships with `@leyman/main` and is on `PATH` automatically. Use `nx` directly — not `npx nx` or `pnpm exec nx`.

See [`AGENTS.md`](./AGENTS.md) for the full skill index.

## CI

This repo uses [Dagger](https://dagger.io/) for CI. To replicate CI locally:

```bash
dagger-test
# or running every task, with no Nx cache:
dagger-test --uncached
```

Run `test-ci` first — it's faster for iteration. Use Dagger to confirm before pushing.

See all aliased (added to `PATH` by [`devcontainer.json`](./.devcontainer/devcontainer.json)) scripts in the [/scripts/commands](./scripts/commands) directory.

## Coding Agents

Agent docs start at [`AGENTS.md`](./AGENTS.md) (also linked as `CLAUDE.md`). In the devcontainer, Claude Code config (credentials, settings, memory) lives in `<main checkout>-worktrees/.shared/claude-config`, outside version control and shared by every worktree. See the [worktrees skill](./.agents/skills/worktrees/SKILL.md).

(If you use a different coding agent, PRs are welcome to support those directories).

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! See [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for setup, conventions and how to submit a pull request. In short:

1. Make your changes
2. Run `test-ci` to verify
3. Run `changeset` and follow the prompts to document your changes
4. Submit a PR — GitHub Actions runs Dagger automatically

This project follows the [Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). To report a security vulnerability, see [`SECURITY.md`](./SECURITY.md).

## Tooling

| Tool | Role |
|------|------|
| [PNPM](https://pnpm.io/) | Package manager with workspace support |
| [Nx](https://nx.dev/) | Task runner with caching and dependency graph |
| [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) | Language (ESM, strict mode) |
| [Go](https://go.dev/) and [Rust](https://www.rust-lang.org/) | Languages of a few projects, such as the `constant-consistent-hash` implementations |
| [SWC](https://swc.rs/) | Fast TypeScript compiler |
| [ESLint](https://eslint.org/) | Linting (opinionated, 15+ plugins) |
| [Biome](https://biomejs.dev/) | Formatting |
| [Mocha](https://mochajs.org/) + [Chai](https://www.chaijs.com/) (via `@leyman/expect`) | Testing, with [Vitest](https://vitest.dev/) for `vitest-chain` |
| [C8](https://github.com/bcoe/c8) | Coverage (100% required) |
| [Dagger](https://dagger.io/) | CI pipeline |
| [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) | Versioning and changelogs |
